National Assembly

Details of the Proceedings

Total
28 Jestha 2083
Thursday
Meeting
Number - 16

Today's meeting of the National Assembly began at 13:21 hrs under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.

Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Members,

(13:21 hrs)
Honourable Members,

Honourable Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr. Shishir Khanal has requested time to speak. I will now provide him with time to speak on a contemporary issue.

Honourable Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr. Shishir Khanal:- Right Honourable Chairperson,

(13:22 hrs)
Honourable Members,

Honourable Chairperson,

Honourable Members,

The government is working with the priority of achieving good governance and economic prosperity, remaining committed to the Constitution, foreign policy, and international relations.

I wish to inform you that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which I lead, is continuously working to protect Nepal's sovereignty, national independence, autonomy, territorial integrity, security, and the rights and interests of Nepali citizens, thereby safeguarding national interests and enhancing the country's image. I have been informing the respected House and relevant committees about the work carried out by the ministry from time to time, and this process will continue. In this context, I will provide information about my recent visit to India and the address made by the Right Honourable Prime Minister to the House of Representatives on 17 Jestha 2083, as well as issues including the Nepal-India border.

Right Honourable Chairperson, Honourable Members, at the cordial invitation of His Excellency Dr. S. Jaishankar, the Honourable Minister of External Affairs of India, I visited India for a three-day official visit from 22 to 24 Jestha 2083 and have returned. I believe that this visit, which represents the new government formed after the elections held last February, has made a significant contribution to further strengthening the friendly and multifaceted bilateral relations between Nepal and India. During this visit, on 23 Jestha 2083, I held an official meeting and delegation-level talks with His Excellency Dr. S. Jaishankar, the Honourable Minister of External Affairs of India, in New Delhi. Comprehensive and fruitful discussions were held on all aspects of Nepal-India bilateral relations during the talks. Specific discussions were held on trade and economic cooperation, connectivity, energy cooperation, water resource management, common security concerns, border management, sports, and enhancing people-to-people relations. Both sides have expressed their commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations. Furthermore, views were exchanged on various regional and international issues. Discussions were also held on reviewing the progress of various bilateral cooperation projects and making them more effective. During the meeting, we made three joint declarations.

(a) Operationalization of cross-border payment for P2P transactions under the Memorandum of Understanding signed between NCHL and NPCI in June 2023. This has opened up a way for citizens of both countries to transfer money digitally within their respective countries.

(b) Virtual handover of reconstruction projects completed with India's development assistance in Nepal after the earthquake. This included the handover of 72 health-related projects and 12 culture-related projects. And (c), a Memorandum of Understanding was signed between Kathmandu University, School of Engineering, Centre for Digital Public Infrastructure and Artificial Intelligence, and Digital India, Bhashini Division for the co-creation of a national digital infrastructure for a voice-first language translation platform. We believe this will provide a foundation for developing large language models for common languages spoken in Nepal and India.

During the visit, I also met and held discussions with India's National Security Advisor, Mr. Ajit Doval. In that meeting, views were exchanged on common security concerns of Nepal and India, border management, and various aspects of cooperation between the two countries. During the visit, I had the opportunity to address a group of eminent persons at a special program organized by the India Foundation in New Delhi. In that program, I shed light on the priorities of Nepal's foreign policy and interacted with the participants focusing on issues of common interest such as energy, trade, and borders. I also inspected the Nepali Embassy in New Delhi and interacted directly with the embassy staff about their recent activities, directing them to work with commitment to protect Nepal's and Nepalis' interests in India. I also informed the media in India about our priorities through a media interaction organized at the embassy.

I feel that the discussions and high-level meetings held during this visit have taken Nepal-India diplomatic and economic cooperation to new heights and have created a strong foundation for moving forward with result-oriented cooperation in areas of mutual interest in the coming days.

This visit has provided an opportunity to express Nepal's balanced, independent, and multifaceted foreign policy more strongly. Through this visit, a concrete foundation has been laid for expanding trade and investment, strengthening energy cooperation, promoting tourism, and further strengthening connectivity and people-to-people relations. Views were also exchanged on contemporary international issues such as regional stability, supply chain security, and energy cooperation.

Right Honourable Chairperson, dozens of bilateral mechanisms have been established to work in various sectors between Nepal and India. Meetings of bilateral mechanisms that have been inactive for a long time have now resumed. Regular meetings of such mechanisms can play an important role in further strengthening relations between Nepal and India by discussing possibilities and areas of cooperation.

I would like to provide information about the upcoming meetings of some important such mechanisms.

First, the meeting of the Joint Working Group (JWG) on Border Management is scheduled to be held in August 2026. Similarly, the Joint Field Survey Team (JFST) has been working in various locations for the past two months. As per the responsibility assigned to this mechanism, the work of repairing border pillars, restoring lost pillars, and reconstructing them is underway. Likewise, four separate teams have been formed and are working in various areas of the Nepal-India border. These joint teams are working to prepare an inventory of encroachments on no-man's land and cross-border occupations. Similarly, the next meeting of the Survey Official Committee is scheduled to be held in August 2026. This will include a technical team from the Department of Survey led by its Deputy Director General, as well as representatives from the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Armed Police Force. The Indian side will also have a similar representation.

Similarly, among some important meetings recently concluded, the meeting of the Joint Commission on Koshi and Gandak Projects was held in Kathmandu on April 30 and May 1, 2026. In this important meeting, held after a gap of four years, discussions were held on studying the problems in the project areas and moving forward with their solutions. Similarly, on May 2, 2026, the Nepal-India Joint Team on Flood Forecast Activities on Rivers Common to Nepal and India meeting was held in Kathmandu. Discussions were held on steps that can be taken to further streamline the early warning system to minimize disaster and loss of life and property during the monsoon, and cooperation has moved forward. Similarly, on May 7-8, 2026, the meeting of the Joint Technical Team on Cooperation on Power Sector was held in New Delhi. Detailed discussions were held in that meeting regarding the expansion of cross-border transmission lines required for electricity trade between Nepal and India. Along with this, meetings of other bilateral mechanisms are also being organized. It is expected that the multifaceted relationship between Nepal and India will become even more consolidated and profound.

Right Honourable Chairperson, now I would like to mention the address of the Right Honourable Prime Minister and the issue of the Nepal-India border. The Right Honourable Prime Minister, on 17 Jestha 2083, during the question-and-answer session in the Federal Parliament's House of Representatives, mentioned the issue of Nepal's border and stated that the government is committed to resolving problems through bilateral dialogue. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs provided detailed information regarding the views expressed by the Honourable Prime Minister on the same day. The official stance of the Government of Nepal regarding India's operationalization of the pilgrimage route through Lipulekh, which is Nepali territory, was clearly stated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on 20 Baishakh 2083.

India's response to the diplomatic note sent by Nepal on this issue has also been received through a diplomatic note from the Government of India. Both countries have expressed their commitment to resolving border-related disputes through diplomatic means and mutual dialogue. It is well known that Nepal and India share a centuries-old open border. The current international border between Nepal and India is primarily established and delineated by the Treaty of Suguali of 1816. The demarcation of the Nepal-India border is yet to be completed in the areas of Susta, Limpiyadhura, Lipulek, and Kalapani. In addition to these areas, problems of cross-border occupation and encroachment on no-man's land exist in some other places.

The issue mentioned by the Right Honourable Prime Minister in the parliament specifically relates to encroachment on no-man's land and cross-border occupation. When determining the Nepal-India border, the fixed boundary principle has been adopted in riverine areas, leading to cross-border occupation where citizens of one country cultivate or reside in the territory of the other country. To manage the long border between Nepal and India in a systematic and scientific manner, technical teams of border-related mechanisms of both countries are active in constructing and repairing border pillars in demarcated areas, collecting data on encroachments on no-man's land, and cross-border occupations. The work of the technical committee, which has been stalled for a long time, is currently active in the border areas, and data collection is being carried out jointly. The Nepal-India Border Working Group (BWG) and other related mechanisms are engaged in mapping to determine the number of places along the Nepal-India border where there is encroachment on no-man's land and cross-border occupation. Detailed information on this will be available later. The study by the technical committee indicates that in some places, land currently under Nepal's use and occupation may fall into India's territory, and land currently under India's use and occupation may fall into Nepal's territory. Both sides claim the land under their respective use and occupation.

The statement made by the Right Honourable Prime Minister in parliament is also related to this technical reality and cross-border occupation. The fundamental question here is how to resolve the border issue. Therefore, in accordance with the spirit and sentiment of the close relationship between Nepal and India, we are always committed to resolving this issue through diplomatic dialogue based on historical treaties, agreements, and maps.

In the course of responding to the issue of Nepal's border in the federal parliament on Jestha 17, 2083, the Right Honourable Prime Minister mentioned the United Kingdom because Nepal's border is directly related to the Treaty of Sugauli in 1816. We have not sought mediation from any third party. The Right Honourable Prime Minister only indicated that if necessary, the use of reference materials from the then-prevailing situation could be helpful in resolving the problem. I want to make it clear to this Honourable House that the Nepal-India border is a bilateral issue. And in the spirit and sentiment of the close relationship between Nepal and India, Nepal is always committed to resolving this issue through diplomatic dialogue and negotiation based on historical treaties, agreements, and maps. Finally, after the formation of the government, we have been working by prioritizing foreign policy and international relations focused on national interest and the country's image. Through high-level visits, bilateral relations are being strengthened, and efforts have been initiated to make bilateral mechanisms with friendly countries active and effective.
I addressed the House of Representatives of the federal parliament on this matter only yesterday. Our main goal is to work by focusing on national interest. Since the management of foreign relations is a sensitive matter, we all have a responsibility, contribution, and role in this regard. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has been performing strongly and effectively in its areas of jurisdiction, and I commit to continuing this in the future and keeping this Honourable House informed about the achievements made. I also look forward to your guidance and bid farewell from here. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, time has been requested to speak on behalf of the parties represented in the National Assembly. I will now provide time to the Honourable members sequentially. First, Honourable member Kamala Pant.
Honourable Ms. Kamala Pant (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, Sir, from the 17th of Jestha until now, we have not been able to advance many important agendas and significant issues. The reason for this is known to the entire House and the entire country. The reason was that the guardian of the nation, the executive head of the country, the Right Honourable Prime Minister, spoke about a very important issue concerning the country, and we were not given a response regarding that. The National Assembly, like the House of Representatives, was not given a response. We were not given a response, neither the opposition nor the ruling party. But it is not as if the opposition has an extraordinary love for nationality and the opposition does not. Therefore, we fulfilled our role and drew attention to the fact that we, the National Assembly, are also serious about the sovereignty of the country. This is the National Assembly, the representative of sovereignty. We stated that the representatives of the people should not remain silent on this matter. Honourable Chairperson, Sir, even though the Chairperson said, "This is an important bill, it needs to be moved forward," we were unable to move it forward.
This means that we are currently in this dignified meeting of the National Assembly. Here are mature leaders, mature politicians, renowned experts from various fields and sectors, and important personalities from political and social life. Elders who have shed blood and sweat throughout their lives to bring this system this far are present here. Therefore, we are aware, serious, and sensitive to the importance given to us by our constitution and the role the country and the people expect from us, and we are not and will not be prejudiced towards any person or institution. The government might think that the National Assembly has no representation from its members. It might seem like there is prejudice. But we are serious and sensitive about our responsibilities, and we are also sensitive to implementing this constitution and ensuring its security and moving it forward. Therefore, I urge that the party that formed the current government does not need to feel any inferiority complex because it has no representation in this parliament, nor does it need to harbour such an inferiority complex. And I request that the government should not be afraid of the National Assembly. The National Assembly is serious. As I said at the beginning, the leadership that has come through a long struggle is present in this House. This House may not have much technical knowledge, but it has political knowledge. Therefore, I request that the government be serious.
We are ready to cooperate with the government. We are not against the government. We are ready to cooperate with the government. But the government should not be so irresponsible. Why irresponsible? Because the Prime Minister is the executive head. Even though the Right Honourable Prime Minister spoke in the House of Representatives yesterday, the Prime Minister spoke... but what is it... I don't think the Prime Minister is limited to the House of Representatives. Our House does not know that, the National Assembly does not know. But whatever the Prime Minister says in any cabinet, the country listens. The country knows. And the entire population of the country understands this responsibility. Therefore, we, the National Assembly, understood this responsibility. We felt we spoke even if we didn't speak here. We felt we spoke by coming here. And we were unable to move this parliament forward. All parties, all parties present in this House were unable to move it forward.
Honourable Chairperson, Sir, regarding the 17th of Jestha, the statement made by the Right Honourable Prime Minister in the meeting of the House of Representatives regarding the border dispute between Nepal and India has not only bowed the heads of the country and its people but has also insulted the great patriots and brave warriors who sacrificed their lives for the defence of the country's borders. Regarding Kalapani, we said yesterday that this is a territory that Nepali youth, Nepali women carrying children in their laps, defended through struggle. We felt that words were spoken that would tear this territory apart. Although the Honourable Minister of Foreign Affairs has now said that this was not the intention, we accept that it was not the intention. May such words not come from the Prime Minister's mind. But what is the guarantee that such words will not come in the future? This is the cabinet's responsibility, or rather, the Prime Minister's prime ministerial system, our system. The Prime Minister's words become law in some matters. Without going into much detail about the Prime Minister's words, what has this intention caused? If India says, "We are enemies with Nepal because Nepal has encroached upon our land," what will happen? How can the Honourable Minister of Foreign Affairs explain that this is not the case, that this is not the Prime Minister's language? It is a serious matter. We do not understand.
We hope that does not happen, and we want that. And the other thing is, how many brave warriors have been martyred? What does the blood of those martyrs say? The government, in particular, must take this into consideration. What is national independence? That language must also be understood. What is national independence? What is sovereign power? What is territorial integrity? How much is our territory, over how many kilometers does it extend, what is the security of its borders? This must be understood. And therefore, the government must not do anything that curtails the rights of the Nepali people, which are the property of sovereignty. My request is this. If an attack comes not from any foreigner but from our own country's executive head, the Prime Minister, what will happen? I still cannot understand whether the Prime Minister will say these things or not. Therefore, we sought the Prime Minister's response, and our demand is still that the Prime Minister's statement should come. We are not saying that this demand has been met now. As I said at the beginning, the National Assembly has a natural responsibility. We are ready to fulfill that responsibility. But that does not mean that our demand has been met today. Politics does not get resolved solely by votes obtained through elections. It is easy to criticize, but very difficult to govern. I will not dwell on many things now.
There were also things the Right Honourable Prime Minister said yesterday. I am aware that he said he is ready to give his life for the integrity of this country. I will not go into that. But there are also instances in our history where many parties have received many votes through elections. It is very recent, no need to look back. There is no need to show such arrogance just because one has received votes. One does not have to say many things just because one has a microphone in front. 
Running the government is also difficult. For a country like Nepal, how important are cooperation, unity, and understanding? Our leaders, cooperation, consensus, and unity... it seems like Girija Prasad Koirala said in 2062/063 that we must move forward through consensus, cooperation, and unity. It seems like it was just now. Our leader, our leaders, from B.P. Koirala, what B.P. Koirala said to Jawaharlal Nehru, what he said when he went to China, the instances where he bowed down saying "Sagarmatha is ours" when others claimed it as theirs, are written in black letters in our history. Without going into that, what I want to request is that we must proceed with understanding. Votes will sometimes be for one person, sometimes for another. I am confident that the government is taking that understanding seriously. I also want to state here that the government should not think that "they have given in again."
Yesterday, there were grievances and hurt feelings among the people. Therefore, the government formed on that basis has also not given hope. The people were very disappointed yesterday. Let's say they sold that disappointment. The current party, which has a majority, which has secured almost a two-thirds majority, has created a narrative, let's say, it has convinced them. It has convinced them, it has secured a majority. But that does not mean it will last forever. It does not mean it will last forever. Therefore, how to proceed is a matter of the government's own consciousness. I request that consciousness should be awakened. We want the government to create an environment where cooperation can be sought. Since the 17th, the party chairman has gone to India, the government has not even started a dialogue. What is this? Can the opposition parties be suppressed like this? Does that happen in politics? What will the world say? Therefore, dialogue is necessary.
As they say, "Bādhebādhe jāyate tatvabodha" (Understanding arises from debate). We must proceed like this. The government, I feel so, and I have also made a request.
Our desire is not a big desire. It is a desire to cooperate with this government. The people are tired. The people who were tired of the change of government are now looking forward to a government with such a large majority, and they are happy. May it run smoothly, we wish it well. We also want to save it from difficulties. Therefore, the government should not be so terrified of us, should not be afraid. The government is built from the unprecedented sacrifice, dedication, and struggle of the people.

May we be honest towards the constitution, laws, and the rule of law. Our hope was that, Honorable Chairperson, after this government came to power, we thought it would uphold the rule of law. I want to mention one thing that pricked me, not out of fear. While the Anti-Money Laundering Act is in place, a law has been made to demand property details, and property details are being sought. Every year, MPs' property details are collected. What happens if we select from that? Why should everyone be terrorized now? I am not saying this out of fear, Honorable Chairperson, but why spread this terror? Was this necessary? Let the rule be by law; we want the rule of law. But this was an irresponsible act. What happened somewhere, who should have spoken in the House of Representatives, perhaps the members of the House of Representatives have not spoken. Who behaved indecently? A committee should have been formed under the convenorship of a senior person. Under whose convenorship will it be formed? Will you go to such a low level of behavior, to the level of an undersecretary? I want to submit that this is wrong. And one must be freed from the delusion of ruling by threatening or coercing parties, communities, or classes, creating state terror, and ruling. In a democracy, to get votes in elections, to win seats, means to be very serious about the country and the people, not to be hasty. One must be serious, and after the people have given their mandate, one must be serious and not be too hasty. But here it is the exact opposite. There is a lot of arrogance and ego visible. That same arrogance is sometimes seen in disrespecting the Honorable President, sometimes in disregarding parliament, sometimes in not even holding essential dialogues, and sometimes in attacking poor and helpless citizens. The state must stop this kind of behavior. Honorable Chairperson, before I conclude my remarks, we have a different character in this parliament, the National Assembly. Therefore, we cannot keep this parliament hostage to indecision. Nevertheless, I request the government to be serious and I conclude. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Jhakk Prasad Subedi. (14:54 PM) 90 Honorable Mr. Jhakk Prasad Subedi (Nepal Communist Party): Honorable Chairperson (13:54 PM) Sir, Honorable Prime Minister Mr. Oli, on the 17th, this very Jestha 17th, from the rostrum of the House of Representatives, he said, "You might find one thing strange, I too only found out after becoming Prime Minister, that India has encroached not only on Nepal's land but also on many places in India." Mr. Chairperson, this statement by the Prime Minister is indecent, condemnable, objectionable, and anti-national. Nepal has not occupied any territory of India. The Prime Minister's statements, given without any study of history, are against Nepal's sovereignty. This statement is an invitation for intervention by a neighboring country. Since 1962, India has established a military camp in Kalapani, a Nepali territory, and encroached upon the land. Is the Honorable Prime Minister aware of this issue regarding Kalapani and 21 other places? This is what is called the height of irresponsibility. In Darbula alone, 37,000 hectares of land have been encroached upon. The Prime Minister has spoken on this issue in a planned and organized manner. When the issue of Kalapani, Lipulekh, and Limpiyadhura arose from the public level, the Prime Minister spoke this to divert the issue. Mr. Chairperson, when the Prime Minister spoke on such a sensitive issue, the nation's sovereignty was endangered, and the country was put in trouble by the Honorable Prime Minister. You might think that by not speaking, I am doing work. You have said it repeatedly, and we have heard it. Were you studying until now without speaking about where Nepal has encroached on India's land? You did not come to the parliament to answer the policy and program, our Honorable Prime Minister. The primary responsibility for the country's sovereignty, integrity, and security is the Prime Minister. He has forgotten that he is the Prime Minister of the country. The Prime Minister has the responsibility to protect the country's territorial integrity. Is it appropriate for a person like the Prime Minister to say that Nepal has encroached on India's land? It is a great misfortune for the Nepali people that a person like Honorable Mr. Oli has become the Prime Minister. Where and how much land has Nepal encroached upon in India? The Nepali people must be informed. Mr. Chairperson, nothing can be compared to the motherland. Love for the country is patriotism. The patriotic spirit is alive in the blood of every Nepali. Honorable Prime Minister, you must apologize to the parliament. The Prime Minister's statement must be removed from the parliamentary record. You have insulted the country. This is a country saved by the blood of our ancestors. The Prime Minister of the country cannot attack the nation and nationality. Rashtriya Swatantra Party (RSP) has a very common saying, "The knowledgeable are beaten." RSP said during the election, "The knowledgeable are beaten." The Prime Minister spoke about something that no one knew until today. Nepal has encroached on India's territory. The Prime Minister, being overly knowledgeable, raised an issue that even India has not raised today, Mr. Chairperson. Honorable Prime Minister, your statement has weakened Nepal's stance with its neighbors regarding the border dispute. The person who governs the state must be politically astute. Otherwise, populism will turn Nepal into Ukraine and Pakistan, and the destination of popularity is fascism. The Prime Minister is the chief executive of the country. Every expression, statement, and decision of yours has an impact at the national and international level. Statements made in a dignified, constitutional, and legal institution like parliament must be responsible, factual, and evidence-based, Honorable Prime Minister? Issues related to Nepal's borders and sovereignty are extremely sensitive and of national importance. Is it permissible for a responsible person like the Prime Minister to speak based on personal assumptions, hearsay, or unverified information on such serious matters? It is not just your ignorance, but a diplomatic crime to give statements contrary to this. The Honorable Foreign Minister further exaggerated what the Prime Minister said in parliament. This is also a new development here. If a minister of the country slips up while speaking somewhere, the Prime Minister corrects it. Here, when the Prime Minister slipped up while speaking, the Foreign Minister tried to correct it by coming here. Mr. Chairperson, is this what is new? He talked about land encroachment, about cross-border occupation. Is encroaching on the border the same as cross-border occupation, Mr. Chairperson? This is a different matter. In a country with an open border, cross-border occupation occurs. When rivers change their course towards Nepal, our neighbors, the Indian communities, cultivate land in Nepal's territory. And if the flow increases towards India, the communities of Nepal go and cultivate there. That is what cross-border occupation means. But has the Honorable Prime Minister spoken about cross-border occupation? He has said that the border itself has been encroached upon. The Honorable Foreign Minister turned day into night here in parliament, Mr. Chairperson. In 1974, a person named Lendup Dorji in Sikkim became a hero overnight. In the election, Lendup's party won all but one seat. Whatever Lendup did, whatever he said, no one opposed him. They only applauded. Mr. Chairperson, finally, Lendup said that Sikkim should be merged with India. All the MPs were banging the tables with both hands. I feel extremely sad to say this. On the 17th in Nepal, when Honorable Prime Minister Mr. Oli said in parliament, "Nepal has also encroached on India's land in many places; I found out after becoming Prime Minister," the MPs from the ruling side were supporting it by banging the tables, and the people of Nepal and the world watched this. Should not the patriotic MPs within RSP, the MPs from the ruling party, speak against the statement of Honorable Prime Minister Mr. Oli? Patriotic MPs, intellectuals, journalists, and the Nepali public are raising strong voices against the Prime Minister's statement. We have also been raising our voices in the National Assembly from the 19th to yesterday. We have fulfilled our role, Mr. Chairperson. Because the Prime Minister of the country has expressed such irresponsible and anti-national views, disillusionment has definitely arisen among the people. If this disillusionment, the disillusionment among the people, explodes, Mr. Chairperson, it will cause a volcanic eruption. We are greatly concerned that its lava will not only destroy this government but will also devastate the political system, as this government is bound to be destroyed. The Prime Minister must apologize. The Prime Minister's statements made in parliament must be removed from the record. Mr. Chairperson, our party, the Nepal Communist Party, is presenting itself as a responsible opposition. We have been thinking of discussing the government's activities, its mistakes, and all the wrong decisions it has made so far, and we will present our views on them later. What I want to state here is that even though we have serious disagreements with the matters spoken by the Honorable Prime Minister, our view was that the Prime Minister should apologize and his statements should be removed from parliament. However, the Prime Minister did not even respond, and his statements have not yet been removed from the record of the House of Representatives. Until the Prime Minister apologizes in parliament and his statements are removed from the record of the House of Representatives, we will continue to protest against this anti-national statement of the Prime Minister in a new way. Our protest will continue, but from today, our parliament will proceed. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: (14:09 PM) Honorable Member Prem Prasad Dahal. 13 Honorable Mr. Prem Prasad Dahal (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honorable Mr. Chairperson, Sir, the address by the Honorable Foreign Minister was heard. I would like to start my topic from here. There will be matters related to the recent visit to India by the Honorable Minister, the neighboring country India. Similarly, he has spoken about discussions on issues like border management and shared security concerns, and that concrete discussions were held. We give the benefit of the doubt. Therefore, when matters have not yet come forward concretely and reached a conclusion, why should we be too critical now? However, regarding the statement made by the Honorable Prime Minister in the House of Representatives on the 17th of Jestha, the Honorable Minister has presented the issue as cross-border occupation and land occupation, and also said that both sides have claims, which we have not heard until today. India is making claims in many places. We are making claims, we are making claims in many places. We are making these claims based on historical evidence, facts, research, and documents. If this was the intention of the Honorable Prime Minister, then why could this not be conveyed to the public? What a misfortune! He has said that the border has been encroached upon. No, it was a slip of the tongue, this is what I wanted to say, my intention was this.

And apologizing to the public after saying these things is even more noble! But that did not happen. What arrogance! What arrogance is this? Not attending parliament, and when attending, disrupting programs that are being addressed by the President of your own government, programs made on your recommendation. Not attending to discuss and interact with the representatives, and not being present to answer their questions and timely queries. This is the situation. Honorable Chairperson, generally the Prime Minister is supposed to be present in parliament for four reasons. One, when presenting the policy and program, which you have already done. Second, when responding to issues raised by members of parliament on the policy and program and when it is passed. Third, in the capacity of a departmental minister, participating in discussions on the Appropriation Bill and discussing issues raised by members of parliament regarding departmental responsibilities such as the Ministry of Defense, the National Planning Commission, and other departmental responsibilities, and getting them passed. Similarly, the Prime Minister is supposed to be present in parliament in connection with the regular question and answer sessions held from time to time. Rather than a system, as a people's representative, it would be much better to be present daily for better discussions and interactions with the honorable members, but that situation did not arise. And the issue he raised on the 17th of Jestha, we obstructed the parliament against that. The National Assembly is different, but in terms of law, we cannot just watch idly when it comes to national interest, geographical integrity, our sovereignty, and our national interest. Therefore, we raised our voice saying that the Prime Minister spoke incorrectly, this needs to be corrected, and he should apologize. In due course, the Honorable Foreign Minister of the Government of Nepal presented his views. Some issues were addressed, an agreement was reached among the parties, our concern is to pass the bill, okay, we will pass the bill, other bills will come, we will deal with them, we will discuss and interact on other policies and pass them, but the most important thing is our national interest. We cannot remain silent on this, we cannot just watch idly, we cannot think that the National Assembly is separate, it is a different world. Therefore, let us also discuss the bills originating from the House of Representatives here, make them better, refine them, amend them, and pass them even better. We obstructed for five or seven days, we will account for that. Therefore, the most important thing for the Nepali people, for us, is national interest and self-respect. Therefore, it became a matter that we had to obstruct, Honorable Chairperson. Now, let me say a few things on this matter. The Nepal-India border is 1880 kilometers long. Our border has been encroached upon in various parts, in many places. 27 districts share a border with India, and border disputes have been reported in 23 districts. India has encroached upon 372 square kilometers of land, including Lipulek, Kalapani, and Limpiyadhura, this is a fact. 144 square kilometers of land in Susta, Nawalparasi district, has been encroached upon. In the process of opening a trade route to Mansarovar via Lipulek, our land is being used unauthorizedly without any inquiry or notification, and we object to this. The government also sent a note, it has done well, and we will praise it if it does well. Large and massive infrastructure has been built on the border. These massive infrastructures, especially the embankment on the Mohana River in Kanchanpur and Kailali districts in the Far West, the Laxmanpur dam on the Indian side, and many other places like the Gandak canal, have seen the construction of high dams, embankments, and irrigation programs. Roads and infrastructure have been built, and especially during the monsoon, the Terai region is completely submerged, and the Nepali people, Nepali farmers, especially Nepali farmers, have had to bear great losses, and the nation has also suffered losses. The nation is also crying there, and the people of the border areas are fighting against it, and we are fighting. This is against international law on the Nepal-India border. This is being done against international law, and India is committing atrocities like this. When our nation, national interest, sovereignty, national independence, and geographical integrity are being compromised, the Prime Minister has made an extremely irresponsible, regrettable, and deplorable statement in the House of Representatives, which cannot be overemphasized. Such a baseless statement has lowered the heads of all patriotic Nepalis. We are extremely concerned about the Prime Minister's statement and express our objection. It shows the height of playing games with the nation. No one, no official, no political leader, no Prime Minister, no border expert, no survey officer, no scholar has ever said what he has said. He has said something that even India itself has not said, that Nepal has encroached upon my land. This is the kind of issue, that it should be specified in which places how much land has been encroached upon, facts should be presented, and that land should be reclaimed. Otherwise, one cannot speak arbitrarily like this. An apology must be made to the public. Either the land should be reclaimed, and it should be identified where and how much has been encroached upon, or an apology must be made to the public. Historical documents, maps, and factual evidence prove that India has encroached upon Nepal's border. Therefore, at a time when geographical integrity and sovereignty need to be protected, it is unfortunate that our own country has made a false statement as if it has encroached upon someone's border. All opposition parties in parliament protested against this false statement of the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister was requested to correct his statement and apologize to the public, but he did not accept this. There can be two reasons for this. First, he believes what he said is true, and second, he is ignoring the voice of the opposition. Even though we raised this issue continuously for some time, the Prime Minister did not attend parliament, nor did he correct his statement. It has been three months since the elections were completed and 75 days since the government was formed, but there has been no initiative from the Prime Minister or the ruling party, or the Government of Nepal, to engage in dialogue with the opposition. Former honorable members have also emphasized this. Forget about national interest, cooperation, and unity, their words, speech, behavior, and style of work show extreme arrogance, pride, and conceit. Even though the government or the Prime Minister is irresponsible, we, the opposition, will not forget our responsibilities that have come to us, and we have the task of passing the budget, passing various bills, solving the daily problems of the people, and bringing those issues to fruition. While maintaining these stances, we have changed the form of our protest. We have done the right thing, the truth will always be the truth, and it will be established over time. The Prime Minister did speak incorrectly in parliament, he did speak, but even after speaking such a wrong thing, he has no remorse or regret. The decisions of a government that has come with such a huge mandate, and the Prime Minister's style of work, behavior, and speech have caused turmoil in the country, and the heads of true nationalist Nepali people have been bowed. We will not compromise on the issue of nationality, and such baseless statements are absolutely unacceptable to us. Therefore, the Prime Minister must immediately correct his statement and apologize to parliament and the general public. We will continuously take the Prime Minister's anti-national statement to the public, and at the same time, we will also resume parliamentary proceedings. What we did yesterday, as I have already stated, we had to do it in the context of national interest, and we did it. Now we have changed the form of our movement. We will continuously take these issues to the public. He did speak incorrectly, because he is not ready to speak afterwards. He should have given an explanation, saying that I spoke this for this reason. I spoke incorrectly, I must apologize to the public, I must give reasons, but such things did not come. Therefore, now this government and... As I have already stated, our parliament will now proceed, our daily activities will move forward, and we will discuss and interact on bills and move forward. However, there are some anti-people decisions made by the government during this period that we must record in parliament, and these are mainly six. First, the bulldozer terror against the landless. Second, our habit of ruling by ordinance and we started that work from there. Unclaimed policy and program, the policy and program became unclaimed. Because the policy and program put forward by the Honorable Prime Minister was presented, and he left, and afterwards, neither taking ownership nor giving an answer on it, this was the situation. That is why I have called it an unclaimed policy and program. Third, the anti-people decision to abolish student unions and trade unions. The issue of Nepal encroaching upon Indian land, and fourth, the issue of changing tax rates in the upcoming economic bill. Looking at all these issues, the government, we want to support it, we have said that we support the government when it does good work, and we are saying it now. When the route to Mansarovar via Kalapani and Lipulek was opened, we were not consulted, and the government sent a note, a diplomatic note, and we thanked them. Do good work, thank you, do bad work, we will criticize. And finally, the extremely traitorous statement made by the Honorable Prime Minister. You should correct yourselves, you should correct yourselves. That statement made by him in time, that statement, in parliament, correcting it will be in his interest. Thank you, Namaste. (14:26 hrs) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Mahanth Thakur. I grant permission to speak from your seat. Honorable Mr. Mahanth Thakur (Loktantrik Samajwadi Party, Nepal): Honorable Chairperson and Honorable Prime Minister... Foreign Minister and Agriculture Minister. Now I have to say something, and I am hurt. And when I talk about my Madhesh, about Tharuhat Madhesh, my voice gets choked, and my eyes start to water. At that time, I am expressing my pain to you. What I have raised now, about 300 years ago, in the west and east of the Yaisi-Chauvisi states, there was Kiprat Rai and Jhum cultivation for the Limbus, and as far as their Kiprat rights extended, the land as far as their eyes could see belonged to them. Everyone accepted this, there was no dispute, and Jhum cultivation belonged to the Limbus, who would change their fields every two or three years. That is why it was called shifting cultivation or Jhum cultivation. In our west...

When they went, the Baise-Chaubisi states were independent states, and they felt freedom, and later they also organized themselves in the form of the Baise-Chaubisi Union. After Mahakali, the 12 and 18 Thakurais, which were in the form of villages, were experiencing freedom like states.

They are not here today. Today we have raised the issue of freedom regarding the Madhesh, and we have raised the same issue regarding Tharuhat Madhesh, but what is the condition of our country? Whatever the Honorable Prime Minister says is law. Every word, every point of his goes into that law. There is no act, no law, no rule, no by-law here. Now, by-laws have been made to work, but they are not followed either. And whatever the Honorable Prime Minister said becomes the law, and we are forced to die, and that compulsion still exists. I experienced something recently: I was doing something in the compound, and many people were dancing and singing. What is this? Lord Shiva was in the middle. How did it become Lord Shiva? That Honorable Prime Minister went to the House of Representatives, and he is also a bit eccentric. When he was leaving, his sandal fell off. And he became Lord Shiva. That is the form of Lord Shiva, isn't it? And that's why there was a commotion there. Now it doesn't happen here, but if it does, I'm here. Lord Shiva also has another form, which is the Tandava dance. When the Tandava dance is performed, it leads to both welfare and destruction. So, in summary, I want to say that welfare is yours, but as far as destruction and devastation are concerned, I am in the battlefield and have not fled from the battlefield. Speaking of these things... we have asked for sovereign power in the power of the state, and we have asked for our government in return for our struggle. We have not asked for struggle, we have asked for our government, and our struggle continues for that, and you can hear that an agitation of sorts is going to start again in the Madhesh within two or three days. Because the thing is, wherever the origin is, the end is also there, and it happens there. And now, Honorable Prime Minister Balen Shah, his ancestors' land is there, Mahottari. Which is now in Madhesh, and now that end has also begun. It will end someday. That is the law of nature, no one can change it. Isn't it? We are going in that state. Now, much (microphone not heard).

Honorable Chairperson:-
(14:34 hrs)
Honorable Mr. Tul Prasad Bishwakarma (Rashtriya Janamorcha):- Honorable Chairperson,
(14:34 hrs)
Today, after the obstruction since the 17th, we finally heard something from the government through the Honorable Minister of Foreign Affairs. For this, I want to thank the government and especially the Honorable Minister of Foreign Affairs, and for a long time, both houses have been seriously disrupted and stopped, and the regular discussions have not been able to proceed as they should.

The main reason for this is the statement of our current Prime Minister, which has created this situation today, and the government had to wait for so many days to correct his statement, and other ministers have been working hard to try to bring his statement back on track. This is definitely a waste of time for the government and also a sad matter for us parliamentarians. We are elected here to make laws in the interest of the country and the people and to advocate for their feelings on their behalf, but we are getting entangled in trivial matters. I hope that such a situation does not arise in the future, and the irresponsible statement he made, which is against the nation, nationality, and territorial integrity, is objectionable, and we have raised this issue repeatedly. I also want to demand that his statement be removed from the parliamentary record and not be repeated in the future.

Honorable Chairperson, we need to look at his statement from different perspectives. So far, the discussion here has been that our Honorable Prime Minister's understanding of Nepal's borders and nationality seems to be limited. We have understood it that way now, and they are protesting him in the same way. But I think there is another side to this. It is possible that he spoke with a lot of understanding, not out of ignorance. Because if we connect the events, he raised the issue of the border on the 17th, saying, "Not only India, but we have also encroached upon India; I only came to know after I became Prime Minister." Some time after that, the chairman of Rastriya Swatantra Party, Rabi Lamichhane, went on a visit to India, and after his visit concluded, now the Honorable Minister of Foreign Affairs has also returned after completing his visit. Is this sequence connected to this statement? Is a long-term plan working behind this? We also need to pay attention to this aspect. Because we know that our southern neighbor, when talking about it, speaks very sweetly, repeatedly talks about the relationship of roti-beti, talks about the elder brother and younger brother, but when any disaster, any political crisis, or natural calamity occurs in Nepal, they repeatedly impose blockades. They trouble the Nepali people by imposing blockades. And when Nepal does not pass things they want for their own interests, when it does not work in their favor, blockades are imposed, which we have experienced. Even when the constitution of 2072 was passed, other countries supported it, but India has not openly supported it yet. Similarly, during the monarchy, other countries supported King Birendra's proposal for a zone of peace, but India did not. There are various incidents and evidence of this kind. Therefore, our neighbor's mind is not that simple. They show sympathy towards Nepal and Nepalis from time to time, and some help is also provided, but we have also experienced that they are always focused on recovering the principal and interest with compound interest for that help. Therefore, I think we need to pay attention to this aspect as well. Because this border dispute is not a new issue; it has been going on for decades. Wherever there are important assets of Nepal, places of strategic importance, India is not ready to resolve the border issue there. The reason why the issues of Susta and Lipulek-Kalapani are still unresolved is their strategic importance. Susta has the Valmiki Ashram. The activity of how to place this Valmiki Ashram on their side has been going on all the time.

Regarding trade with China, India's use of the Lipulek-Kalapani route is not for religious pilgrimage. Because there are many routes from Nepal for religious pilgrimage. It has been going on for centuries, and no pilgrims have been stopped from going to Mansarovar. But why was it necessary to open this Lipulek pass and Kalapani? Because it is a place of strategic importance. It is said that they stayed there after being defeated and returning from the war with China in 1962, and King Mahendra reportedly allowed them to stay there for some time. But later, they have occupied it by building permanent settlements and buildings. This is definitely an encroachment. Therefore, keeping these things in mind, it is the supreme duty of all Nepalis to strengthen and empower Nepal's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and nationality, and to keep it intact. And no matter which faction, which political party, or which ideology we belong to, the first priority is the country, the nation.

As long as we cannot protect the country and the nation, none of our rights, none of our honor, peace, or dignity can be protected. Therefore, we must be serious about this. While saying this, we must also pay attention to the fact that there has been a harmonious relationship between the Nepali people and the Indian people at the people's level for centuries, and we are confident that this relationship will continue in the future and will remain so. However, from time to time, changes in government in both countries and the political leadership that comes to power, their interest towards Nepal, no matter which party comes to power, their view, their understanding towards Nepal never changes. It remains the same. Therefore, we must distinguish this. At the government level, especially with the current BJP government, the process of looking at Nepal has been continuously increasing. Therefore, Honorable Chairperson, I would like to conclude my brief remarks here by urging to correct such statements, remove them from the record, and ensure that such statements are not repeated by individuals in responsible positions in the future. Thank you.

Sir, my question to the Honourable Minister is as follows:
Nepal is an agricultural country. It is the season when all farmers here are busy in their fields and farms. It is the time for transplanting paddy and weeding maize. In such a time, people have to wait in line all day to find chemical fertilizer, and there is always a shortage. What plans does the Honourable Minister have to prevent this from happening this year? Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Minister.
(2:52 PM)
Honourable Minister of Agriculture, Forests, and Environment, Ms. Gita Chaudhary:- Honourable Chairperson
(2:52 PM)
Sir, and all Honourable Members present, I wish to answer the question posed by Honourable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar regarding the supply and current status of chemical fertilizer. I especially wish to thank the questioner Honourable Member from the bottom of my heart.

Mr. Chairperson, Sir, as we are all aware, the Government of Nepal has been providing chemical fertilizer on a subsidy basis to farmers based on cost sharing. In the current fiscal year, 558,522 metric tons of fertilizer have been supplied so far, and 468,016 metric tons have been sold and distributed to farmers. I wish to inform you that there are 138,802 metric tons of fertilizer in stock, including those in warehouses and those that have arrived in Nepal but are yet to be entered into the warehouse inventory. I wish to inform you that by the end of Ashad this fiscal year, a total of approximately 600,000 metric tons of fertilizer will be provided to farmers on a subsidy basis, which will be the largest quantity to date.

Honourable Chairperson, Sir, to ensure there is no shortage of fertilizer during the upcoming paddy transplantation season, the Ministry is making various efforts and preparations. In this regard, I wish to inform you that the suppliers with whom fertilizer supply agreements have been made have been urged to supply the fertilizer on time. As a result, the Ministry expects 90,000 metric tons of fertilizer to arrive in Nepal from the end of Ashad to the month of Shrawan.

24
Similarly, through the G2G procurement channel with friendly India, the Cabinet has granted in-principle approval for the purchase of 80,000 metric tons of fertilizer. In the first phase, the procurement process for 30,000 metric tons of urea and 20,000 metric tons of DAP has been initiated, and this quantity of fertilizer is expected to start arriving from the month of Shrawan.

Honourable Chairperson, Sir, informative messages have been disseminated across the country emphasizing the balanced use of fertilizer and the use of organic and biological fertilizers. Furthermore, to ensure that all farmers receive fertilizer without discrimination and easily, and to prevent potential misuse of subsidized fertilizer, the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests, and Environment has issued a circular to the provincial governments, local levels, and district administration offices across the country to effectively implement the Subsidized Fertilizer Distribution Management Directive, 2082, and to coordinate as necessary to make the fertilizer distribution process easy, transparent, and organized.

Honourable Chairperson, Sir, the fertilizer management information system has been brought into use so that the public can view the status of fertilizer quotas, stock levels of subsidized fertilizer sold through cooperatives and other dealers, and details of farmers receiving fertilizer. Similarly, it is mandatory for fertilizer sellers and dealers to update the details of fertilizer distributed in the Ministry's fertilizer management information system.

After we provide information, they hold a meeting, inform the relevant local levels, and then we distribute the fertilizer. I wish to inform you that we distribute fertilizer until the end of Ashad.

Regarding the fertilizer industry, the work is progressing with our Ministry of Industry and Ministry of Finance. You can check our online system and our website to see where and how much fertilizer has gone. We have disseminated data from the Sudurpashchim Province yesterday, and today we are providing data for other provinces as well, indicating how much fertilizer is in which depot and which local level has collected it and which has not. You, anyone, you and I, and the general public can view the details of where the fertilizer has gone from our fertilizer depots on our website. This is all I have to say for now. sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The meeting of the National Assembly commenced at 13:21 hrs under the chairmanship of Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal. Honourable Minister for Foreign Affairs Mr. Shishir Khanal requested time to speak on a contemporary issue.

speakers.name: Narayan Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Opening the session and granting speaking time

speakers.name: Shishir Khanal
speakers.topic: Requesting time to speak on contemporary issues

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The Minister for Foreign Affairs, Mr. Shishir Khanal, provided a detailed report on his recent official visit to India from 22-24 Jestha 2083. He highlighted discussions on bilateral relations, trade, connectivity, energy, water resources, security, border management, and people-to-people ties. Three joint declarations were made concerning cross-border payments, reconstruction projects, and a language translation platform. The Minister also reported on meetings with India's National Security Advisor and his address to eminent persons in New Delhi.

speakers.name: Shishir Khanal
speakers.topic: Report on India visit and bilateral relations

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The Minister for Foreign Affairs discussed the outcomes of his India visit, emphasizing the strengthening of diplomatic and economic cooperation. He also outlined upcoming meetings of bilateral mechanisms, including the JWG on Border Management, JFST, and Survey Official Committee, and reported on recently concluded meetings concerning the Koshi and Gandak Projects, flood forecasting, and power sector cooperation.

speakers.name: Shishir Khanal
speakers.topic: Bilateral mechanisms and upcoming meetings

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The Minister addressed the issue of the Nepal-India border, referencing the Prime Minister's statement in the House of Representatives. He reiterated the government's commitment to resolving border disputes through diplomatic dialogue and mentioned the official stance on the Lipulekh issue. The Minister explained that while the 1816 Suguali Treaty delineates much of the border, demarcation is pending in Susta, Limpiyadhura, Lipulek, and Kalapani, with issues of encroachment and cross-border occupation in other areas.

speakers.name: Shishir Khanal
speakers.topic: Nepal-India border issues and diplomatic resolution

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The Minister further elaborated on border issues, explaining that cross-border occupation occurs in riverine areas due to the fixed boundary principle. He detailed the ongoing work of technical teams in mapping, pillar repair, and data collection regarding encroachments and occupations. The Minister noted that technical studies might reveal land currently used by one country falling into the other's territory, leading to claims from both sides.

speakers.name: Shishir Khanal
speakers.topic: Technical aspects of border issues and land claims

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Concluding his remarks on the border, the Minister stated that the Prime Minister's parliamentary statement pertained to technical realities and cross-border occupation. He reaffirmed Nepal's commitment to resolving border issues through diplomatic dialogue, respecting historical treaties, agreements, and maps, in line with the close relationship between Nepal and India.

speakers.name: Shishir Khanal
speakers.topic: Commitment to diplomatic resolution of border issues

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The government clarifies its stance on the Nepal-India border issue, emphasizing it's a bilateral matter to be resolved through diplomacy based on historical treaties and maps. The Prime Minister reaffirms the government's commitment to prioritizing national interest and strengthening international relations through high-level visits.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honourable member Kamala Pant criticizes the government's handling of the border issue, stating the Prime Minister's remarks have insulted national heroes and compromised sovereignty. She urges the government to be serious, avoid prejudice, and engage in dialogue, emphasizing the National Assembly's role in safeguarding national interests.

speakers.name: Kamala Pant
speakers.topic: Critique of PM's border remarks, sovereignty, and dialogue

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: A member expresses concern over the government's actions, questioning the necessity of demanding property details and the rationale behind certain investigations. The member criticizes the government for creating terror and acting irresponsibly, urging for governance based on law and order. Another member, Jhakk Prasad Subedi, strongly condemns the Prime Minister's statement about Nepal encroaching on Indian territory, calling it anti-national and a threat to sovereignty. He demands an apology and removal of the statement from parliamentary records.

speakers.name: Honorable Chairperson
speakers.topic: Presiding over the session and calling members to speak.

speakers.name: Jhakk Prasad Subedi
speakers.topic: Condemning PM's statement on border encroachment and demanding apology.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Member Jhakk Prasad Subedi continues his strong criticism of the Prime Minister's statement regarding Nepal encroaching on Indian land, labeling it as irresponsible, anti-national, and a diplomatic crime. He argues that such statements weaken Nepal's position in border disputes and calls for the Prime Minister to apologize and have the statement expunged from parliamentary records. The member announces that his party will continue their protest if demands are not met but will resume parliamentary proceedings.

speakers.name: Jhakk Prasad Subedi
speakers.topic: Criticism of PM's statement, demand for apology, and protest continuation.

sections.summary_en: Member Prem Prasad Dahal begins by acknowledging the Foreign Minister's report on his visit to India, mentioning discussions on border management and shared security. He then addresses the Prime Minister's controversial statement about cross-border occupation and land claims, expressing skepticism about India's alleged claims and questioning why the Prime Minister could not clarify his intentions to the public if he meant something else.

speakers.name: Prem Prasad Dahal
speakers.topic: Discussing Foreign Minister's visit and PM's statement on border issues.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Members of parliament express strong dissatisfaction with the Prime Minister's recent statement regarding border issues, accusing him of irresponsibility and making baseless claims that undermine national sovereignty. They demand an immediate correction and apology. The discussion then shifts to broader government actions, including alleged anti-people decisions and the handling of border disputes with India.

key_issues: Prime Minister's statement on border issues

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: A member raised concerns about the Prime Minister's statements regarding national borders and sovereignty, suggesting a potential hidden agenda. The member also highlighted historical instances of India imposing blockades and questioned the strategic importance of certain border areas. The discussion emphasized the need to protect national integrity and sovereignty.

speakers.name: Tul Prasad Bishwakarma
speakers.topic: Prime Minister's statements, national borders, India's role, national integrity

sections.name: Other Business
sections.summary_en: The Chairperson announced the receipt of letters from the Office of the President regarding the authentication of two bills and the formation of a new Council of Ministers with portfolio allocations. The Minister of Youth, Labor and Employment was noted to be attending an event in Geneva.

bills_discussed.name: The Bill on the Election of Members of the House of Representatives (First Amendment), 2083

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: A notification regarding the temporary assignment of the Ministry of Youth, Labour, and Employment to the Minister of Industry, Commerce, and Supplies due to the absence of the Minister was read out. The Chairperson then announced the commencement of the Question and Answer session related to the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests, and Environment.

speakers.name: Suman Raj Arjyal
speakers.topic: Notification of ministerial responsibility assignment

sections.name: Questions
sections.summary_en: Honourable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar questioned the Minister of Agriculture, Forests, and Environment about the government's plans to ensure adequate chemical fertilizer supply for the upcoming paddy transplantation season and to prevent shortages. The Minister responded by detailing current supply, stock levels, and planned imports, including G2G procurement from India. She also highlighted efforts to ensure transparent distribution and the use of a fertilizer management information system.

speakers.name: Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar
speakers.topic: Chemical fertilizer shortage and supply plans

speakers.name: Gita Chaudhary
speakers.topic: Chemical fertilizer supply status and plans

sections.name: Questions
sections.summary_en: Honourable Member Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar asked a supplementary question regarding the timing of fertilizer supply and the long-term solution of establishing a domestic chemical fertilizer industry. The Minister of Agriculture, Forests, and Environment clarified the ongoing distribution efforts, the expected arrival of new fertilizer shipments, and the progress on exploring a Green Urea technology, while also mentioning the dissemination of fertilizer data through online systems.

speakers.name: Bhuwan Bahadur Sunar
speakers.topic: Fertilizer supply timing and domestic industry

speakers.name: Gita Chaudhary
speakers.topic: Clarification on fertilizer supply and industry

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The Chairperson invited the Finance Minister, Dr. Swarnim Wagle, to present a proposal for a general discussion on the Annual Estimate of Revenue and Expenditure for the Fiscal Year 2083/084. The Finance Minister presented the proposal. Dates for the general discussion and the Finance Minister's response were announced, and members wishing to participate were asked to register.

speakers.name: Dr. Swarnim Wagle
speakers.topic: Proposal for budget discussion

key_issues: Annual Estimate of Revenue and Expenditure

sections.name: Adjournment
sections.summary_en: The Chairperson announced that the next meeting of the National Assembly would be held on Friday, May 29, 2083 BS, at 1:15 PM, and adjourned the current meeting.
